source.original_title: 05/18/2026 - Eran Avshalom Ovsiovich & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/18/2026 - Eran Avshalom Ovsiovich & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: London, UK; previously lived in Bangkok, Krabi and Korat, Thailand

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me a little bit of an overview. He said you were a very cool guy.' Prospect: 'The purpose is, as I told Kim, to give you the information', and later 'It's whatever I send Kim. Kim is texting me on WhatsApp.'

prospect.name: Eran Avshalom Ovsiovich
prospect.occupation: Founder of a sales and marketing creative agency helping startups tell their story, opened roughly a year ago. Previously a lawyer, then a copywriter at McCann, then spokesperson for a government minister, then a newspaper columnist, then twelve years in tech including six and a half years at Google.
prospect.training_background: Training for 20 to 21 years, largely self-directed. Was very skinny when young and found gaining muscle slow. Lost condition during COVID gym closures, which he found depressing, and began exploring calisthenics and other modalities via Instagram. Engaged a professional coach for the first time post-COVID — remote, plan-based, tracked in a spreadsheet with YouTube links for form — and went solo again after three or four months once he understood the programme. Has done CrossFit and found it drove him to over-train and get injured. Switched to full-body training two years ago and prefers it. Recently began kettlebell work off Trevor's videos and reports mobility gains. Trains at least three times a week and lasts about 15 minutes on a full kettlebell session.
prospect.medical: Reports recurring exercise-related injuries in the present tense — 'I'm keeping having injuries' — attributed to CrossFit and to ego-driven loading rather than to any named condition. Previously woke with a stiff back; stretches daily. No diagnosis given and none asked for on the call. Has general blood work done every four to six months and reports results are good.

signals: Ran a structured competitive process before the call: 'I was following him and other, like, four guys and I reached out to three just to get them standing, know, what's the plan, what's the value. How much it costs, blah, blah, blah, and then to make a calculate decision'
Self-directed and capable over two decades, and explicitly graduated from his only previous coach after three months — 'after I understood whatever I need to do, I went by my own'
Rejects the offer's core positioning as not applying to him: 'they do need a mentor, I less need a mentor, I need more of a coach'
Wants to buy components rather than the system: 'In my specific position, would probably take bits and pieces, not everything, because I'm already educated'

Optimizer overlay is real — successful, health-literate, fine-tuning rather than rescuing — but the deciding trait on this call was comparison shopping against a functioning free alternative, and he took the cheaper option

goals.text: Fine-tune the physique change he has already started seeing from switching to kettlebells
Build mobility now so he is still mobile in his 50s and 60s
Shorten his training sessions — get a full workout into 20 or 30 minutes rather than 90
Improve cardio and recovery so he is not wiped out after 15 minutes
Stop getting injured by learning correct technique and progression on a new modality
Have a modality that still works if gyms close again

pains.text: Recurring injuries from training, which he attributes to ego and over-intensity rather than ignorance
Lost muscle during COVID gym closures and found it depressing
Declining motivation to spend 75 to 90 minutes in the gym
A gap between his mental age of 30 and his biological age of 45, with mobility as the pressure point
Faces a real learning curve on kettlebells — cannot complete ten minutes of Trevor's prescribed work
A problem with sweets, self-policed by whether his abs are visible
Capital constrained as a one-year-old agency founder allocating funds
Fear of missing out on time that cannot be recovered — 'the worst feeling ever... is missing out. Because you will get to a point at a certain time that you can't take time back'

objections.raw_quote: So it is an interesting, uh, amount... And I need to think about it. And I'll get back to either you or Kim or whatever you're going to guide me with that answer, for sure. But it is substantial. Again, not criticizing your pricing, but that's why I wanted to understand what's the ballpark.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the objection and reinforced it — 'As I said, it is substantial... It's probably like for most people, if they set a budget aside, it's probably not in your budget.' No isolation, no financial questions, no payment plan. He had already pre-empted the objection before quoting, telling the prospect 'it probably won't be in line with your budget.'

objections.raw_quote: I will think about the price and I will either get back to you or to Kim. You will guide me to whom to reach out to.
objections.rep_response: Challenged it directly and effectively — the strongest single move on the call: 'To think about it either typically means, I'll be honest with you, I don't really want to do it, but I'll be really polite. Or it means I'm really, really not sure. But either one, it's uncertain, you know?' This produced a fully honest answer. He then did not press further and moved to the downsell.

objections.raw_quote: In my specific position, would probably take bits and pieces, not everything, because I'm already educated, if I can say that, a bit.
objections.rep_response: Not addressed as an objection. The rep agreed with the framing around coach versus mentor terminology and moved on to pricing.

objections.raw_quote: maybe for now, as the next step, I need to find like a middle ground, either to choose a different service that is costing me less or... To try to build something again on my own, like plan-wise.
objections.rep_response: Supplied the cheaper alternative himself rather than defending the value: 'I can shoot you over the middle ground. We have a middle ground solution if you want to have a look at it.' Screen-shared the $200/month self-guided tier in detail, including the weekly live class with Trevor, and agreed to send the link.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'in 6 months we guarantee that you will go from, let's say your starting weight is 15kg, we guarantee that by the end of the 6 months, with the 3 main kettlebell lifts, that you will be doing it with an 8kg heavier kettlebell... And if you're not doing the eight kilos heavier, we'll work with you until you are.' Correctly stated in kilos with a 16kg-to-24kg illustration, with no pound conversion error.

prospect_financials.note: Stated that $6,000 'would have been the highest training plan I've ever paid in my life' and that as a one-year-old agency founder he needs to work out how to allocate funds. No financial question was asked at any point; the rep instead pre-declared that the price would not fit his budget.

evidence: No decision on the core offer and no explicit refusal: 'I need to think about it. And I'll get back to either you or Kim'

He did effectively decline the $6,000 tier for now — 'maybe for now, as the next step, I need to find like a middle ground' — so if close rate is measured on the core offer this should be read as a loss on that offer

The conversation continues on a different product: he asked for the $200/month self-guided link twice and said 'That might be more relevant for me' and 'this is more [relevant] if I want to be completely transparent with you'
Delivery mechanism agreed — the link to be sent via Kim on WhatsApp
No payment taken, no payment link sent for the core offer, no follow-up call booked and no date set
outcome.next_step: Rep to have Kim send the $200/month self-guided tier link over WhatsApp. Prospect to consider both the core price and the self-guided option and revert to either the rep or Kim. Nothing scheduled.

notable.note: The clearest downsell in the batch: a prospect quoted $6,000 was routed by the rep to a $200 per month product, screen-shared in detail, with the link to follow. That is the second time in this folder the same move has been made, after the Peter Louis call earlier the same week. Two things make it more significant than a lost deal. First, the $200 tier was described here as including a weekly live class with Trevor — thirty minutes training together plus thirty minutes of Q&A, roughly twenty people — while the $6,000 one-to-one tier was described to Luis Ortiz two days earlier as including no calls at all. On the descriptions given, the cheap product has more live founder access than the expensive one. Second, the rep pre-emptively devalued his own offer twice, before and after quoting it: 'it probably won't be in line with your budget' and 'it's probably not in your budget.' On process, the deep phases were absent again — no consequence frame for the seventh consecutive call, no commitment check, and no bridge to motivation, despite the prospect volunteering a fully formed consequence statement of his own: 'I'm seeing people who didn't work out in the 50s, 60s, they look like a wreck. And I don't want to be there.' The one strong move was the challenge to 'think about it', which produced complete candour.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion. The block at 00:14:00 opens under the rep's label with the prospect's sentence about wanting a blueprint and then runs the entire rep philosophy pitch inside it. The pricing exchange at 00:24:25 to 00:24:47 alternates wrongly, with the rep's figures landing under the prospect's label and the prospect's clarifying question under the rep's. The self-guided walkthrough from 00:30:26 to 00:33:13 is similarly split. Several jokes clearly belonging to the prospect — the Bentley line, the OnlyFans aside and the closing remark about Kim — sit under the rep's label. Roles read from content throughout.
